conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: The advocate case was tested and fails. The matched figure exists and is readable: P-273's MRI-only arm, 'cross-validated with identical settings' (Fig. 4B caption, p. 7), measured at AUC 0.8017 and accuracy 0.7598 (calibration within 0.0013). The strongest case for yes is the literal one-way test: 0.802 lies outside P-65's Hanley-McNeil interval [0.808, 0.872], by 0.005-0.008 across the reading range 0.800-0.803. It does not carry the pair. (i) The recorded gap has P-273 higher. P-273's own ablation shows that its clinical inputs produce that gap: MRI-only 0.802 is below P-65's 0.840, and MRI+clinical reaches 0.940. The brief says a pair fails condition 3 when a paper shows an explanation to be sufficient. (ii) The residual runs the other way and is not beyond uncertainty in both directions. P-65's 0.840 lies inside P-273's MRI-only interval [0.741, 0.862], z = 1.09. The matched accuracies agree both ways: 0.760 is inside P-65's Wilson [0.746, 0.814] and 0.782 is inside P-273's [0.702, 0.810]. (iii) P-65 prints its own run-to-run SD, 0.0297 across five repeats 'using identical data partitions' (p. 6), which is training variability on fixed data. Adding the SE of the five-run mean (0.0297/sqrt(5) = 0.0133) to the Hanley-McNeil SE (0.0165) gives a combined SE of 0.0212 and an interval of [0.799, 0.882], which contains 0.802. The one-way crossing does not survive the variability P-65 itself reports.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Met for the recorded figures: 0.962 [0.934, 0.990] against 0.840 [0.808, 0.872]. On the matched figures, only the one-way Hanley-McNeil AUC crossing above is met.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds. 0.962 is below 0.97. P-65 has 573 subjects and an external OASIS-3 cohort (0.8137).

results.reason: The reader's MRI-only reading is confirmed by an independent pixel measurement (0.8017, calibrated within 0.0013 against printed values). The one route to yes is the literal one-way test on the matched AUC: 0.802 is outside P-65's Hanley-McNeil bound 0.808. That residual is reversed relative to the recorded gap. P-65's value lies inside P-273's matched interval (z = 1.09), the matched accuracies agree both ways, and the crossing disappears once P-65's own printed run-to-run SD is included. P-273's ablation shows its added clinical inputs account for the recorded gap, so the pair fails condition 3.

conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: The reader left condition 3 open because 'the paper prints no number' for P-273's MRI-only arm. The value is readable from Fig. 4B, and the matched figures agree within uncertainty. Pixel measurement, calibrated within 0.0013 against seven printed or text-derived values, gives MRI-only AUC 0.8017 and accuracy 0.7598. AUC: P-273's 0.802 lies inside P-356's Hanley-McNeil interval [0.634, 0.846]. P-356's 0.74 sits on P-273's MRI-only lower bound, which is 0.739-0.742 across the reading range 0.800-0.803, so no crossing can be established; z = 0.99. P-356's own whole-brain 3D ResNet-18 (AUC 0.75, SD 0.01) is the input representation nearest P-273's 3D volume, and it lies inside both intervals ([0.646, 0.854]). Accuracy: 0.69 lies 0.012 below P-273's MRI-only Wilson interval [0.702, 0.810], while 0.760 lies inside P-356's [0.586, 0.778]; z = 1.22. That crossing comes from class balance, not discrimination. P-273's MRI-only operating point, read from the same figure (sensitivity 0.511, specificity 0.907), gives 0.756 at its own 91/238 pMCI share, which reproduces the bar, and 0.718 at P-356's 41/86 share. The Wilson interval for 0.718 at n = 238, [0.658, 0.772], contains 0.69. So the papers' own data dissolve the gap. Removing P-273's clinical and genetic inputs takes the AUC from 0.962 to 0.802, which is 0.16 of the 0.22 gap, and the 0.06 residual is within uncertainty on AUC in both directions.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Fails. The advocate case: the task and comparison match (prevalent Petersen-type MCI against non-MCI in Chinese hospital inpatients), the channel matches (clinical/questionnaire), and P-307 sets a diabetes-based model's AUC (0.893) beside its own. Against it: the rule requires the same population class behind the label and gives a disease-defined patient population (Parkinson's patients) as a different class. Here each sample is defined by a different disease, chronic pain at age >= 60 (mean 71.1) against hospitalisation for T2DM from age 40 (mean 60.2), and each model rests on disease-specific predictors. P-307 itself treats the diabetic population as a separate target population whose model does not serve its own. P-270 states that its diabetic predictors are 'specifically limited to the diabetic population'. On the sources, the two papers address MCI identification in two different patient populations.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Fails under the AUC reading. The advocate case: both papers print AUCs for MoCA-based MCI against non-MCI in Chinese community adults from questionnaire data. P-261's limitations call its model 'the prediction model', and condition 6 directs judging printed figures rather than the record's AUC-against-OR comparison. Against it: P-261's stated objectives are association (to compare prevalence and to 'analyze the ... association' of sleep characteristics with MCI). Its AUCs are fit statistics for exposure models built from a DAG, and the paper says 'The smaller the values of AIC and AUC, the better performance of the model', so it does not offer its AUC as a discrimination result. The brief lists 'the association of a named factor with MCI' as a separate question from 'MCI against controls'. P-261 addresses the first and P-258 (a risk nomogram) the second.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Under the AUC reading, AUC with AUC. As recorded, AUC against OR, which is a mismatch.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Fails under the sleep reading, the one question both address. P-261: PSQI sleep disturbance, adjusted OR 1.681 (1.231-2.296). P-258: sleep quality and insomnia were not significant in univariate screening, with the statistics only in Multimedia Appendix 1 and no estimate in the paper. That is a difference in significance alone, which Section 5.2 does not count. Under the AUC reading the derived intervals do not overlap: 0.835 [0.797, 0.873] against 0.682 [0.645, 0.719].
conditions_attacked.6_record: The record misreads the metric (it computes a gap between an AUC and an OR). Judged on printed figures, the result is as above.

results.reason: The strongest case for yes is that both papers print AUCs for MCI against non-MCI in Chinese community adults with non-overlapping derived intervals (0.835 [0.797, 0.873] against 0.682 [0.645, 0.719]), and P-261 calls its model a prediction model. But P-261 is an association study whose AUC is a model-fit statistic it misreads ('smaller ... better'), so it offers no result on the detection question, and condition 1 fails. On the shared association question (sleep), P-258 prints no estimate, a difference in significance only, which fails condition 4.
